intro: A wider palette of feelings, and the verbs that build them: dar, ponerse, sentirse and hacer.
p.alivio.consejo: It comes from «aliviar». You say «sentir alivio» or «¡qué alivio!».
p.orgullo.consejo: The adjective is «orgulloso» and takes «de»: «estoy orgulloso de ti».
p.angustia.consejo: Here the «u» is pronounced: «an-GUS-tya». The adjective is «angustiado».
p.envidia.consejo: You say «tener envidia de» someone or «dar envidia»: «me da envidia tu viaje».
p.agobiado.consejo: Its noun is «el agobio». There is also the verb «agobiarse».
p.avergonzado.consejo: Careful: «embarazada» is not «embarrassed»; it means expecting a baby.
p.ilusionado.consejo: False friend: «ilusionado» means looking forward, not believing something false.
p.hacer ilusión.glosa: to be exciting, to look forward to
p.hacer ilusión.consejo: It works like «gustar»: «me hace ilusión el viaje».
p.dar pena.glosa: to make sad; to be a pity
p.dar pena.consejo: It works like «gustar»: «me da pena irme». With another person: «me da pena que te vayas».
p.dar pánico.consejo: Like «gustar»: «me da pánico volar». Who feels it is «me», «te», «le»…
p.dar asco.consejo: Like «gustar»: «me da asco el pescado crudo». What disgusts is the subject.
p.ponerse furioso.consejo: «Ponerse» + adjective marks a quick change: «me puse furioso».
p.emocionarse.glosa: to be moved, to get emotional
p.emocionarse.consejo: It takes «se» and often goes with «con»: «me emocioné con tu carta».
b1.titulo: Four ways to build a feeling
b1.texto:
**1. Dar + noun.** It works like «gustar»: what causes the feeling is the subject. **Me da asco** el pescado crudo; **me da pánico** volar; **me da pena** irme; **me da envidia** tu viaje.

**2. Ponerse + adjective.** A quick change: **se puso furioso**, **me pongo nervioso**.

**3. Sentir and sentirse.** **Siento** alivio and orgullo; **me siento** aliviado, orgulloso, agobiado.

**4. Hacer ilusión.** Something you look forward to: **me hace ilusión** el viaje.

If a second subject appears, the verb goes in the **subjunctive**:

- **Me da pena que** te **vayas**.
- **Me hace ilusión que** vengáis.

**False friends.** **Avergonzado** is «embarrassed»; **embarazada** means expecting a baby. **Ilusionado** means looking forward, not having false «illusions».
b2.f0.texto: They have given me the job in Valencia.
b2.f1.texto: I am very proud of you.
b2.f2.texto: It makes me sad that you are leaving.
b2.f3.texto: But I am really looking forward to starting afresh.
b2.f4.texto: I get emotional every time I think about it.
b2.f6.texto: And I am terrified of making a mistake.
b2.f7.texto: When you start, you will feel great relief.
b3.titulo: Feelings and how to say them
b4.texto:
**Dar** + noun: **me da pena**, **te da miedo**, **le da asco**. The person who feels goes in **me, te, le, nos, os, les**.

**Ponerse** + adjective: a quick change of mood. **Se puso furioso.**

**Sentirse** + adjective: how you are. **Me siento orgulloso.**

**Hacer ilusión**: you look forward to it. **Me hace ilusión el viaje.**

With a **second subject**, the subjunctive: **me da pena que te vayas**, **me hace ilusión que vengáis**.
b4.e1.texto: He got furious when nobody told him.
b4.e2.texto: I am looking forward to you coming to see me.
b5.f0.texto: For three months I lived overwhelmed among notes and cold coffees.
b5.f1.texto: That morning, on opening the page with the results, I felt a distress that took my breath away.
b5.f2.texto: My heart beat in my throat like a frightened bird.
b5.f3.texto: When at last I saw my name on the list, I was moved and began to cry.
b5.f4.texto: An immense relief ran through my body like a warm wave.
b5.f5.texto: Then I thought of my disappointed classmates and felt a little ashamed.
b5.f6.texto: My father, who hardly ever says anything, hugged me very tight.
b5.f7.texto: He told me in my ear that he was proud of me.
b5.f8.texto: Now I am really looking forward to starting a new life.
b5.f9.texto: Even so, it makes me sad to leave my city.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «avergonzado» is someone who feels shame.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It is a false friend: «embarazada» means expecting a baby.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Ilusionado is looking forward, not feeling shame.
b7.pregunta: How do you say «embarrassed» in Spanish?
b8.frase: Me hace mucha ilusión que vengáis
b8.traduccion: I am really looking forward to you coming
b9.o0.refuerzo: That is it: a feeling with a second subject takes the subjunctive.
b9.o1.refuerzo: It is indicative, and here you need the subjunctive.
b9.o2.refuerzo: It is the future indicative; after «que» comes the subjunctive.
b9.pregunta: There is a second subject: choose the mood.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «ponerse» + adjective marks a quick change.
b10.o1.refuerzo: That describes his character, not a sudden change.
b10.o2.refuerzo: That says how he is, not how he changed.
b10.pregunta: Which tells a sudden change of mood?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: ilusionado is looking forward with hope.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That would be a mistake; the word is about looking forward.
b12.o2.refuerzo: It is the opposite: decepcionado is feeling let down.
p.orgullosa.consejo: It is the feminine of «orgulloso» and takes «de»: «orgullosa de ti».
p.vayas.consejo: Subjunctive of «ir». The «v» sounds «b» and the «y» as in «yo».
p.ilusión.consejo: The accent marks the last syllable. The plural is «ilusiones», with no accent.
p.emociono.consejo: It is the «yo» form of «emocionarse». The «c» sounds «th» before «i».
p.pánico.consejo: The accent marks the first syllable: «PÁ-ni-co». The «c» sounds «k» before «o».
p.equivocarme.consejo: «Equivocarse» plus «me»: the pronoun attaches. The «qu» sounds «k».
p.sentirás.consejo: Future of «sentir»: it has an accent because the stress falls on the last syllable.
p.asco.consejo: «Dar asco» means to cause a strong rejection. The «sc» is read «s-k».
p.puso.consejo: Irregular past of «poner»: «puse», «puso». «Se puso furioso» means he changed mood.
p.furioso.consejo: The feminine is «furiosa». With «ponerse»: «se puso furioso».
p.avisó.consejo: The accent marks the last syllable. The «v» sounds «b».
p.vengáis.consejo: Subjunctive for «vosotros». The «g» before «á» sounds as in «gato».
p.verme.consejo: «Ver» plus «me»: the pronoun attaches to the infinitive. «Venir a verme» is to visit me.
p.agobiada.consejo: It is the feminine of «agobiado». Its noun is «el agobio».
p.cafés.consejo: Plural of «café». It keeps the accent: «cafés».
p.notas.consejo: Here they are exam results. They are also notes you write, or musical notes.
p.sentí.consejo: Past tense for «yo». The accent marks the last syllable: «sentí».
p.cortaba.consejo: «Cortar la respiración» means to take someone's breath away. «Cortaba» is the imperfect.
p.respiración.consejo: It comes from «respirar». It ends in «-ción»; the plural is «respiraciones».
p.latía.consejo: The accented «í» breaks the diphthong: «la-TÍ-a». It is said of the heart.
p.emocioné.consejo: The accent marks the last syllable. It is the past for «yo».
p.inmenso.consejo: The feminine is «inmensa». It means very big.
p.recorrió.consejo: The «rr» rolls strongly. The accent marks the last syllable: «recorrió».
p.tibia.consejo: Neither cold nor hot. The masculine is «tibio». The «b» and «v» sound the same.
p.pensé.consejo: Past for «yo»: the accent marks the last syllable. «Pensar en» someone is keeping them in mind.
p.decepcionados.consejo: Plural of «decepcionado». The «c» sounds «th» before «e» and before «i».
p.avergonzada.consejo: It is the feminine of «avergonzado». It comes from «vergüenza», with a diaeresis.
p.abrazó.consejo: For «yo» the «z» becomes «c»: «abracé»; for «él» it stays: «abrazó». The accent marks the last syllable.
p.oído.consejo: «Al oído» means very close to the ear, in secret. The accent splits the diphthong: «o-Í-do».
p.muchísima.consejo: Superlative of «mucha»: more force. The accent is on the «í»: «muchísima».
p.ganas.consejo: «Tener ganas de» something is wanting to do it. It is almost always plural: «tengo ganas».
